ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image shows a benzene ring on the left with two adjacent substituents: an oxygen substituent on the upper adjacent ring carbon and a carbonyl-containing acyl substituent on the lower adjacent ring carbon. The carbonyl carbon is bonded to a three-membered epoxide ring. The epoxide contains one oxygen atom and two carbon atoms; the right epoxide carbon is bonded to a phenyl ring on the right. Curved arrows and the α/β labels are present but are to be ignored. Reasoning: The left fragment is therefore an ortho-oxygen-substituted benzoyl group, represented as O=C(c1ccccc1O). The carbonyl carbon is directly connected to one carbon of the epoxide, which can be written as C1OC1. The other epoxide carbon bears the right-side phenyl substituent, c1ccccc1. Combining these connectivities gives the SMILES expression O=C(c1ccccc1O)C1OC1c1ccccc1.

Identify the left fragment as an ortho-oxygen-substituted benzoyl group: a benzene ring attached to a carbonyl carbon, with O on the adjacent ring carbon. Then follow the covalent path from the carbonyl carbon to the three-membered epoxide ring, and from the other epoxide carbon to the right phenyl ring. Translate this connectivity into SMILES by starting at the carbonyl oxygen/carbon, writing the substituted aromatic acyl group in parentheses, then writing the epoxide ring and terminal phenyl substituent: O=C(c1ccccc1O)C1OC1c1ccccc1.
